concerns.text: T019 mandates storing 'full RAW synthetic data trajectories (all raw data points per iteration)' for the full sweep. This violates SC-004 (6h runtime, 7GB RAM) and the plan's memory constraint (<6GB). Storing 1000 iterations × 6 ρ × 4 n × 4 p × 5000 features × 4 bytes exceeds terabytes, making the task physically impossible under the spec's constraints. The task silently relaxes the feasibility constraint by demanding storage that breaks the system.

T010 explicitly states the memory monitor 'does NOT raise an error' if RSS > 6GB. This violates FR-009 which mandates the system 'MUST detect... and apply regularization... or raise a specific error code'. By opting out of the error path for a critical failure mode, the task weakens the functional requirement.

T028 implements a 'permutation test generator' but omits the critical constraint from FR-004 that the test must 'respect the correlation structure'. Without this explicit instruction, an implementation could use naive permutation, breaking the Gold Standard reference and violating the core research validity defined in the spec.

Phase 6 tasks (T033-T035) implement 'Failure Mode Explorer' and 'Embarrassing the Theory' deliverables. These specific artifacts and the 'jagged line' visualization are not present in spec.md (FR-001 to FR-009) or plan.md. This constitutes unauthorized scope creep, adding work not authorized by the specification and violating the constraint that tasks must not introduce features absent from the plan.

T032 stores bootstrap CIs but does not mandate storing the permutation reference p-values or raw KS comparison data. SC-001 and FR-004 require the KS statistic to be measured 'against the permutation-based reference'. Without storing the reference data, independent verification of the measurement (Constitution Principle I) is impossible, effectively weakening the reproducibility requirement.
